sections.title: Sample deck and edit rule tests
sections.what: Builds a one-slide sample deck and runs four tests. They check that edits stay separate from the source and record old wording, that bad batches change nothing, that page budgets are checked on the final result, and that new budgets are capped.
sections.why: The test names state the rules this feature must keep, so each rule has its own test.
sections.watch_out: The tests hard-code budget numbers, so changing a limit means updating these tests too.

summary: Automated checks for the rules of editing slide wording: edits stay separate from the source, bad batches change nothing, and text budgets hold.
purpose: Guard the presentation edit rules against accidental breakage.
why: The test names state the rules being guarded. Any further reason is not stated in the code.
how: Each test runs the edit function on a small sample deck and checks the result with assertions. First, it checks wording edits stay isolated and record the old wording. Second, it checks a bad batch changes nothing. Third, it checks page budgets on the final batch. Fourth, it checks new budgets are bounded.
inputs: A built-in sample deck with one slide, one fact and citations, plus several lists of edits.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each of the four tests, reported by the Node test runner.
risks: The tests cover only four rules. Passing them does not prove the router or database code works. The sample data is simpler than real decks.
debug: Run this file alone so one failure is easy to see. A failed assertion shows the expected and actual value. If a budget test fails, compare its numbers with the limits in the edit module.
